title: Flip a Char Array in Place
statement: You get an array chars of single characters. Reverse their order in place: change the array you were given, using only O(1) extra memory. Return nothing.

examples.why: Swap the outer pair, then the inner pair. With an even length every character moves.
With an odd length the middle character stays put. Here the whole array is symmetric, so it looks unchanged.

constraints: Each entry is a printable ASCII character
hints: The first character must end up last and the last must end up first. What about the second and the second-to-last?
Each swap fixes two positions at once. When can you stop?
Put one pointer at each end, swap, and move both inward until they meet or cross.

explain.intuition:
Reversing pairs position i with position n − 1 − i. Swapping each such pair once does the whole job, and a swap needs only one temporary variable, so memory stays O(1).

Two pointers walk in from the ends and swap until they meet. You must stop at the middle: walking all the way through swaps every pair twice and puts the array back the way it was.
steps: Stop when they meet; the middle element of an odd-length array stays where it is.
pitfalls: Looping i over the whole array instead of half. Every pair gets swapped twice and nothing changes.
Building a reversed copy and reassigning the parameter (chars = [...chars].reverse(), or chars = chars[::-1] in Python). That changes the local name, not the caller's array.
Writing chars[i] = chars[j]; chars[j] = chars[i] without a temporary, which copies one value over the other.

solutions.title: Reversed copy written back
solutions.idea: Copy the array reversed, then write the copy into the original slots. Simple, but it uses O(n) extra memory, which the problem forbids.

solutions.title: Two pointers swapping inward
solutions.idea: Swap the outermost unsettled pair and move both pointers toward the middle.

followups: Reverse the order of the words in a char array in place, keeping each word readable. (Hint: reverse twice.)
Write it recursively. What does recursion cost in memory here?
